upper_a:
Use case: ui-mockup. Design a premium INDIAN AGRICULTURE EDUCATION and ADMISSION-GUIDANCE platform called AGRICO. This is a section-by-section visual redesign of an existing education homepage, not a different product. The user wants individually designed, generously developed sections like a professional college-admission platform. They rejected generic green reskins, identical card stacks, a vegetable marketplace and dashboard layouts. The approved idea to preserve is B.Sc. Agriculture VERSUS B.Tech. Agricultural Engineering, compared with useful academic differences. Make agriculture and agritech visible through DEGREE CONTENT, STUDENT LEARNING, ACADEMIC ILLUSTRATIONS and technical study themes. Keep real course/university discovery and counselling. No commodity or vegetable imagery, no grocery catalogue, no sidebar app shell, no fake stats, fees, ranks, institutional seals, partnerships or job guarantees.
OUTPUT: one flat front-on high-fidelity desktop webpage screenshot of the UPPER HALF of a complete homepage, with SIX fully developed sections, plus global header. Portrait around 1536 x 2560, or enough height for these sections to be readable. Use a 1320px-wide implied desktop content grid, generous section padding, 18px body and strong 32px section headings. Do NOT squeeze a whole 12-section homepage into this one image. No footer yet; page continues below. No devices, browser chrome, board labels or repeated tiny text. Section numbers below are instructions, not labels to print.
DESIGN DIRECTION A — ACADEMIC FIELDBOOK.
Forest #174C35, leafy green #39764C, warm ivory #FBFBF4, pale sage #EAF1E4, restrained pale lime #D6E6A2. Clear sophisticated sans-serif, substantial academic typography, 8px corners, fine botanical-technical linework, precise rules and bespoke mono-line study illustrations. Green with air and warmth, not flat institutional boilerplate. A consistent subtle curriculum/field-notebook visual language across sections. No giant serif slogans. Each section must have a distinct composition while the typography, buttons, spacing and strokes stay coherent.

HEADER: white, original open-book + small leaf "agrico" identity, subtitle "Agriculture Education & Admissions". Nav Programmes, Universities, Compare, Admissions, Guides, search icon, Sign in, green Talk to a counsellor.

1 HERO / PROGRAMME FINDER:
A balanced refined ivory/soft-sage hero, compact relative to the page, about 380px implied height. Left dark-green heading "Agriculture degrees." / "Clearer decisions." Support "Explore programmes, compare universities and plan your admission." A useful real finder below: small tabs "B.Sc. Agriculture", "Agri Engineering", "Horticulture", "Agribusiness"; search "Search programmes, universities or locations"; green "Find programmes". Right ONE thoughtfully cropped photograph of adult Indian university students with notebooks and a laptop in a contemporary agricultural university learning space, campus/lab architecture visible. A restrained academic line graphic of a microscope and engineering schematic subtly integrated around the image, not an arch cutout, product collage or floating dashboard. It should immediately read higher education.

2 GUIDANCE SERVICES:
One integrated slim white ribbon, three well-balanced cells with tiny consistent academic icons: "Explore degrees", "Compare universities", "Get admission guidance". No three giant generic cards.

3 PROGRAMME EXPLORER — THIS SECTION NEEDS ORIGINAL UI:
Heading "Choose your agriculture study path." Left short copy and a small undergraduate/postgraduate selector. On the right TWO substantial elegant COURSE-PATH PANELS side by side, not four identical generic cards.
Panel one: small chapter tag "SCIENCE PATH", title "B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture", three curriculum topic pills "Plant science", "Soil science", "Crop studies". Tiny original line illustration of a student at a microscope. Bottom metadata "Undergraduate" and "Campus learning"; View programme arrow and Compare checkbox.
Panel two: chapter tag "ENGINEERING PATH", title "B.Tech. Agricultural Engineering", topic pills "Farm systems", "Soil & water", "Food processing". Tiny original academic line drawing of a student working on an engineering model. Same useful actions, but composition balances the first panel.
Below both panels, TWO refined compact additional programme rows across the section: "B.Sc. Horticulture" and "MBA Agribusiness", with level chips and View programme links. No plant-product pictures or identical marketing boxes. Emphasise actual academic decisions.

4 UNIVERSITY DISCOVERY:
Heading "Choose the university behind your degree." Three considered UNIVERSITY STUDY CARDS across. Simple pale-sage monogram tabs "PAU", "TNAU", "IARI", full names Punjab Agricultural University; Tamil Nadu Agricultural University; ICAR-IARI. State labels Punjab; Tamil Nadu; Delhi. Useful link group in each card "Programmes", "Campus & learning", "Admissions". One "View university →" action. A small section-level "Compare universities" link. No generated official logos, fake campus photos, rankings or learner counts. These should feel like academic dossier cards, with fine borders, purposeful data and distinct hierarchy, not blank placeholder tiles.

5 AGRICULTURE + TECHNOLOGY — BESPOKE ACADEMIC FEATURE:
A beautifully designed horizontal sage notebook/blueprint feature, not a generic promotional banner. Left eyebrow "LEARNING BEYOND THE CLASSROOM", heading "Where agriculture meets technology." Short support "Explore the science, engineering and practical learning behind modern agriculture." Centre an original refined forest-green mono-line illustration: a university student and instructor at a workbench studying a drone model and soil/water engineering diagram, with subtle crop-research context on a small screen. This is EDUCATIONAL illustration, not a machine shop or sales page. Right three useful study-theme links with tiny diagram icons: "Precision agriculture", "Soil & water systems", "Food engineering". Clear "Explore related programmes →" action. Make this section as polished and distinctive as an illustrated engineering degree feature.

6 THE IMPORTANT COMPARISON — GIVE THIS SECTION ROOM:
Heading "Agriculture or Agricultural Engineering?" and support "Compare what you will study before choosing a degree." One properly art-directed two-programme ACADEMIC COMPARISON, not a tiny 3-row box.
Column headings are substantial, same width: "B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture" on pale sage; "B.Tech. Agricultural Engineering" on soft forest with white text. Small original science/engineering line icons, no folder tabs. Below, exactly aligned rows with a left row-label rail and legible useful differences:
"Study focus" — "Agricultural sciences" versus "Engineering applications".
"Core subjects" — "Plant, soil & crop sciences" versus "Machinery, water & food systems".
"Practical learning" — "Laboratory & field studies" versus "Design labs & technical projects".
"Career areas" — "Research, extension & agribusiness" versus "Engineering, irrigation & processing".
"Entry requirements" — "Check programme eligibility" on both, as links.
An integrated green footer strip in this section: "Find the programme that matches how you want to learn." and "Open full comparison →".
All academic text must be concise and readable; make the comparison aesthetically strong, useful and completely finished. Do not add a page footer or compress the six sections. Deliver exactly this upper homepage screen.

Academic notebook-inspired fine rules and original scientific/student mono-line illustrations. Every section has a distinct purposeful composition but belongs to one coherent education platform.

7 ADMISSION JOURNEY:
Title "From course choice to campus." A spacious designed horizontal THREE-STEP learning-to-admission route with elegant green numbered chapter markers, not three generic floating cards: "01 Explore your programme", "02 Compare universities", "03 Get admission guidance". Each has a concise meaningful support line and useful small action link. Add a narrow adjacent warm-white "Before you apply" mini checklist with "Review eligibility", "Check official information", "Prepare academic records". Keep the section calm, practical and beautifully aligned.

8 PRACTICAL LEARNING — A BESPOKE AGRICULTURE EDUCATION SECTION:
Title "Look beyond the degree title." Small support "Explore the learning, facilities and practical work behind each programme." Build an excellent original LEARNING MAP section: LEFT about two thirds contains three horizontal academic pathways with tiny precise line icons and connected topic labels, not dashboard charts:
"Science laboratory" → "Plant & soil studies" → "Explore B.Sc. Agriculture".
"Engineering studio" → "Water, machinery & processing" → "Explore Agri Engineering".
"Field learning" → "Research, observation & projects" → "Explore university facilities".
Use thin connecting rules and clear arrow links, so students see the connection between study and practice. RIGHT one-third a natural realistic photograph of adult Indian college students and an instructor in a university laboratory reviewing a notebook and microscope, framed cleanly on pale sage. No crop-product thumbnails, no claims that every university has identical facilities. This section should feel like a course-adviser designed it.

9 STUDENT KNOWLEDGE / GUIDES:
Title "Know more. Choose better." One featured education guide on the left with a restrained student-at-study photograph and title "Agriculture or Agricultural Engineering?" A right stack of two beautifully typeset guide rows: "What to check in a university" and "Preparing for admission counselling". Small labels Course choice / Campus checklist / Admission planning, concise descriptive lines, clear Read guide arrows. Original editorial hierarchy, not three identical photo cards.

10 NEWS & LEARNING UPDATES:
A sophisticated compact note-board section with two generous horizontal rows separated by fine rules, not fake breaking-news cards. Heading "From agriculture education". Row themes "Learning precision agriculture at university" and "Inside agricultural engineering workshops". Tiny labels Learning / Practical skills, document icons, small "Read update →" links. No invented current dates, admissions-open notices, student counts or testimonials. These are illustrative education content titles.

11 FAQs:
A proper spacious two-column FAQ section. Left title "A little more clarity." with small contextual course/university/admissions links, right FOUR clean accordion rows:
"How is Agriculture different from Agricultural Engineering?"
"How can I compare university programmes?"
"Where do I check eligibility?"
"How do I get admission guidance?"
Use consistent green plus or chevron icons, refined borders and generous spacing. No giant campaign copy.

12 COUNSELLING CALLBACK:
A polished final forest-green section with excellent visual balance and adequate room. Left heading "Let's plan your next academic step." Short support about programme choice and university guidance; an original quiet pale-lime line illustration of an adult student and academic counsellor reviewing a course sheet. Right a properly aligned WHITE CALLBACK FORM with visible labels "Full name", "Mobile number", "Programme of interest", a small contact-consent checkbox and one forest/lime "Request a callback" button. This is an education counselling service, no job or admission guarantee. Make this section as considered as the hero, not a generic dark block.

FOOTER:
Crisp warm-white footer, thin forest divider, original agrico book/leaf wordmark, four small link groups Programmes / Universities / Admissions / Contact, a short education-platform description, tiny 2026 copyright. No huge scenery or vegetables. The final screenshot must look like the professional finished continuation of the referenced upper homepage.
